title: LONGQAEVAL: Designing Reliable Evaluations of Long-Form Clinical QA under Resource Constraints

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing system-level quality ratings from coarse (document-level) versus fine-grained (sentence-level) annotations to demonstrate how fine-grained evaluation mitigates the tendency of annotators to unfairly favor longer, more elaborated model-generated responses over shorter, concise physician answers.

Analyzing human preference for the formatting and contextual elaboration typical of LLM-generated answers compared to direct physician responses, and showing how constraining evaluation to sentence-by-sentence analysis reduces this confounding effect.
